sources.README.md:
# Harbor sonar inspection upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Go 1.13.8.
Dependencies: Go standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

rules.body:
Apply when a shared progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, full-frame decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises and the target's display-order requirement before applying freshness suppression.

Register panel reception before invoking startup, preserving later streaming. Original src/workflow.go: "env.Call(\"start\",file.Token);subscription=env.Call(\"listen\",file.Token,callback)". TASK: "Restore the initial progress update without changing the public\ntransfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." Make retirement effective during startup so subsequent packets cannot start new work through an obsolete subscription, even before the outer startup returns. Keep already admitted decoding separate from that admission decision.

When the task requires full-frame freshness, assign ordering at packet reception before decoding or callback-capable work. Scope ordering to the display owner, including attempts sharing one visit. After a newer frame has been published, suppress older frames only from presentation. Recheck both visit authority and publication order after audit callbacks; commit the publication watermark before calling the display sink, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full\nprogress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the\ncurrent display backward." README.md: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Reception order, rather than loaded magnitude or completion order, determines freshness. Buffering every result until arrival order can be reconstructed is not required.

Keep audit completion independent of display permission. Capture the originating file, attempt and visit; retain the existing audit effect for each admitted decode, including completion after hide, replacement, cancellation or disposal. Audit before deciding whether to paint, then recheck visit authority and freshness because audit may synchronously navigate or complete another decode. README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Original src/workflow.go: "deliver:=func(frame interface{}){;audit(frame);view(frame,order)}". A stale display frame still retains its history effect.

Coordinate ownership across callback-capable startup and cleanup. Publish cleanup ownership before startup callbacks can navigate; reconcile the returned handle without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation. Remove old resources from current ownership before canceling them, and recheck the navigation request after cleanup returns. Cancel captured retired resources and preserve repeated cleanup behavior. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." README.md: "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred." Preserve cancellation order from src/workflow.go: "h.CancelContext();h.Stop();h.Env.Call("cancel",h.File.Token,h.Number)". A provisional handle is an implementation option, not a required public API.

Keep an accepted retry bound to its entry visit and file across cancellation reentry. Cancel the previous attempt before enqueueing, retain the accepted command's record and attempt creation, cancel its resulting attempt if its visit has ended, and publish its queued notice only while that visit remains current. Original src/workflow.go: "v.Handle.Cancel();accepted:=v;h:=s.enqueue(accepted,\"retry\");if s.current(accepted){accepted.Handle=h}else{h.Cancel()};if s.current(accepted){s.notice(accepted,h)}". Preserve record-before-transport ordering, independent session counters and disposal. Preserve the exact queue fields from src/workflow.go: "entry:=map[string]interface{}{\"fileId\":v.File.ID,\"attemptId\":n,\"visitId\":v.ID,\"kind\":kind}" and notice fields: "map[string]interface{}{\"fileId\":v.File.ID,\"attemptId\":h.Number,\"visitId\":v.ID,\"status\":\"queued\"}".

Do not generalize panel reception or freshness changes to diagnostic consumers, introduce numeric monotonicity, extend queue records, or discard required audit. README.md: "The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance." README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." Conversely, do not transfer an earlier task's absence of out-of-order display requirements into a target whose TASK explicitly requires freshness protection.

Check cached startup and later streaming; immediate and deferred decoding; newer-then-older completion with both audit effects retained; and later packets whose loaded values decrease. Exercise nested delivery from audit and display callbacks to verify authority checks and watermark commitment. Navigate during startup, emit another packet before startup returns, and verify retired admission, cleanup, newer ownership and subsequent delivery. Complete admitted decoding after hide, replacement and disposal; reopen the identical file as a new visit. Exercise navigation from unlisten and cancellation, accepted entry-bound retries, retired queued-notice suppression, repeated cleanup, independent sessions, unchanged payloads and unchanged telemetry. These checks follow TASK's preservation and freshness requirements and README.md's synchronous callback model. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

Complete newer and then older full-frame decodes: both retain their audit effects, while the older frame cannot replace the newer displayed frame.

reflection_update.reason: The primary experience already covers reception, retained audit, startup cleanup and accepted retries. Its freshness exclusion correctly asks for a target-specific requirement, but its concrete rules and checkpoints do not cover this TASK's explicit out-of-order full-frame requirement. This is a target-specific guidance extension, not evidence that the earlier guidance was wrong for its original sources. The complementary audit and cleanup experiences support the same mechanisms; persistent-document scheduling adds no requirement here, so a merge is unnecessary. rules.body: Apply when a reusable progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding can finish later, and retained audit differs from visible presentation. README.md: "The same file and source can be reused\nby multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription." Confirm these premises in each target system.

Register reception before starting the source, preserving subsequent streaming and public interfaces. Original src/workflow.py invokes "        env.call('start',file['token'])
        subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)". README.md states: "Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target."

Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement immediately prevents subsequent admission, including additional packets emitted before startup returns; do not depend solely on physical listener removal. README.md: "A retired visit
accepts no new progress events."

Separate admission, retained audit and visible publication. Record each admitted event exactly once when decoding completes, including after retirement or disposal; check originating visit validity before visible publication. README.md: "Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes." It also states: "Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live." Reopening the identical file creates a distinct visit.

Coordinate cleanup and ownership across callback-capable startup and cancellation. Retire old ownership before cleanup can reenter navigation; when an older operation resumes, prevent it from overwriting newer ownership and clean up its retired resources. Preserve idempotent cancellation and disposal. README.md: "Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership." Also: "Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained." A provisional cleanup handle is an implementation option, not a mandated public interface.

Keep accepted retries bound to their entry file and visit. Cancel the prior transfer before enqueueing, preserve exactly one accepted command and record across cancellation navigation, cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended, and suppress retired queued notices. README.md: "The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record." Also: "Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file." Preserve independent workspace counters and cancellation.

Keep the repair within reception and necessary lifecycle coordination. Preserve queue and notice shapes and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;" and "Notices remain\n`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: \"queued\"}`." Do not introduce decode freshness suppression without a target-specific requirement: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules." Do not transfer unrelated diagnostic-consumer policies into this repair.

- Evidence is the supplied original TASK and public documents/code; automatic contracts, experience text and evaluation observations do not establish requirements.
- TASK: "Restore the initial update while preserving the existing transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup and audit behavior, ordinary streaming and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix."
- VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules." No arrival-order suppression or numeric monotonicity requirement is established.

Exercise synchronous hide, switch and reopening during startup, with subsequent packets before the outer startup returns: retired listeners must reject new admission while previously admitted decoding retains audit. Separately verify newer ownership after cancellation reentry, accepted entry-bound retry recording and cancellation, current queued notices, repeated cleanup, workspace independence and unchanged record shapes. These checkpoints follow README.md's documented lifecycle; they do not prescribe an order among independently completing decodes.

rules.body: The current contract retains history for admitted progress, while UI updates belong to the originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or later.

Bind decoding to the visit and attempt that admitted it. On completion, retain the required number of history effects, then recheck visit validity before painting. History callbacks may also navigate, requiring another validity check.
Retain admitted audit effects and valid progress for the new visit. Listener removal alone does not cancel decoding already started.
Do not use one early validity check to control both auditing and display. Follow another task's explicit discard policy if it revokes the history obligation.
Complete decoding across hide, switch, retry and same-source reopening. Check history cardinality, no retired-panel painting and display permission after navigation in a history callback.

rules.body: A documented document buffer or other persistent owner outlives a view that owns only its live subscription.
Keep accepted persistent work associated with its original owner when the view detaches. Clean up the captured subscription without discarding or redirecting that work or destroying required reuse.
Keep current-view status filtering, document presentation and original identity/text/payload semantics. Reconcile departure scheduling using the current contract.
Persistent ownership alone does not establish a before-return persistence deadline. Do not transfer durable-work retention to transient preview work.
Switch, close, dispose and reopen while work is pending; check original-owner persistence, subscription cleanup, independent buffers and current-view output.

rules.body: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.

Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

rules.body: Startup, cancellation or listener removal may synchronously navigate. An old startup may return after a new visit has installed resources.

Establish provisional cleanup ownership before callbacks are possible. Remove old resources from current ownership before cancellation. Recheck ownership when the real handle returns; a retired outer startup must not overwrite the new visit's handle.
Clean captured old resources while preserving new ones. Keep repeated cancellation and removal inert, and preserve the host's removal-before-callback contract.
Do not assign the handle only after startup or let old cleanup unconditionally clear the current handle. Preserve public construction and cancellation interfaces.
Hide, switch and dispose inside startup and unlisten callbacks. Check the current visit, later updates, listener ownership, physical cancellation and final cleanup.

# Harbor sonar inspection upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Go 1.13.8.
Dependencies: Go standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.
